claims.text: Sonar research engineer Antonio Aversa published an instrumented trace of one ordinary 800-line pull request: 512 model round-trips, 106,000 fresh input tokens, 3.1 million cache-write tokens, 152.8 million cache-read tokens, and 289,000 output tokens, roughly 156 million tokens billed for about $41.
In the Sonar trace, about 98% of billed token volume (152.8M of 156M) was cache re-reads of context re-sent on each of the 512 turns.
Sonar's median cost is $52 per PR (one repository's number); at that rate a 25-engineer team shipping 40 PRs a week is a six-figure line item that no seat count predicts.

Martin Alderson's modelling from published price cards finds five times the agent turns costs nine to seventeen times as much, and cutting turns by 10% reduces cost per agent run by around 16%, because the cache-read term grows quadratically with turns.
Anthropic prompt caching bills cache reads at 0.1x base input price, 5-minute cache writes at 1.25x and 1-hour writes at 2x, with the read charged on every request that uses the cached content.
Artificial Analysis measured Fable 5.1 at $3.76 per Intelligence Index task versus $3.14 for Fable 5 (20% more per task), because the newer model emits about 1.7 times as many output tokens.

Augment Code recommends spend per merged change as the unit: total fleet spend (provider consumption and service fees) plus supervision hours at a loaded rate, divided by agent-attributed changes merged in the period; use spend per completed task for fleets that do not merge.
Cosmos routes each conversational turn to a model through Prism at 20 to 30% lower cost per task while preserving frontier quality.
Uber's engineering team decomposes agent spend into six multiplying terms: users, sessions per user, turns per session, requests per turn, tokens per request, and price per token.

Augment recommends chargeback or showback by gate owner (the review lead holding a service's merge gate), and warns that ranking engineers by token consumption (a leaderboard, 'tokenmaxxing') rewards agent overhead rather than merged changes.

Augment recommends a pooled monthly platform ceiling owned by the VP Engineering with finance, spend tiers with manager sign-off on upgrades, and a cheaper default model for well-defined subagent tasks with manual override for frontier reasoning.
Layered budget controls for autonomous agents include a per-iteration cap of typically 2,000–4,000 tokens and a per-run budget typically $5–$25 depending on task complexity.

A small-to-large fallback cascade starts each request at the cheapest plausible tier and escalates on low confidence; it consumes tokens twice on escalated requests but cuts overall cost 60–85% where 70–85% of requests are handled by budget models.

A per-PR review cost of $0.12 versus $1.40 across agents reflects differing tool calls and context sizes rather than brokenness; cost per completed task should be charted over time to detect regressions.
Attributing a whole session at the primary model's price overcharges by 30–60% for workflows that route heavily to cheaper models, so the ledger must record the model per inference call.

Ignoring cache write costs under-attributes cost by 20–40% for sessions with long system prompts; cache write cost (1.25x) paid by one project's pipeline can leave a later project a windfall at 0.1x unless an amortization policy is set.
Recommended practice is a 90% model-downgrade threshold before the 100% hard cap, since hard stops leave tasks in inconsistent states; P95 rolling forecasts achieve ±8–12% accuracy.

GitHub Copilot (June 2026) moved to monthly AI Credits at $0.01/credit based on token usage with pooled budgets and admin controls at enterprise, cost-center and user levels; per-repository attribution is not native.
Organizations with tiered model architectures achieved a median blended cost of about $2.31 per million tokens versus roughly $18.40 for routing everything to frontier models, an eight-fold gap.
Semantic caching typically saves about 30–50% on repetitive workloads, and an LLM gateway enforces hard spend caps at virtual-key, team and organization level plus rate-based circuit breakers.
On Claude Sonnet 4.6, cache reads cost $0.30 per million tokens versus $3.00 standard; break-even is 2.3 reuses of the cached prefix within the one-hour TTL.

Timestamps in a system prompt break caching: one team with a 60,000-token RAG prefix got a 1% discount instead of 90%, and OpenClaw issue #19534 showed a 170,000-token context reprocessed each request at roughly 10x expected cost.
Monthly API costs per engineer ran $500–$2,000, and agentic workflows consume 5 to 30 times more tokens per task than a chatbot query.
In CloudZero's worked example, routing 8 of 12 steps from Sonnet 5 to Haiku 4.5 cuts a task from $0.132 to about $0.088, a 33% reduction.

A Gartner note reported by The Register says nine in ten agent workflow steps are routine and open-weight models can run them at as little as a twentieth of the cost, but Gartner estimates the realistic saving at five to six times per task.
